title: Engaging Children of Drug Offenders to Mitigate Risks of Them Becoming Drug Offenders
what_it_is: Engaging Children of Drug Offenders to Mitigate Risks of Them Becoming Drug Offenders

sections.label: Preventive measures for drug offenders' children
sections.summary: Asked whether the Government systematically engages drug offenders' children in preventive programmes and what metrics evaluate their effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Government undertakes systematic preventive measures to engage the children of drug offenders in programmes that aim to mitigate the risk of these children becoming drug offenders themselves in future; and (b) if so, what criteria or metrics are used to evaluate the effectiveness of such programmes.

sections.label: Vulnerable children of inmates referred
sections.summary: Vulnerable children of inmates needing education support or counselling are identified and referred to community programmes, with over 1,200 YRCP volunteers reaching more than 15,000 families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: They also identify vulnerable children of inmates who may require support in their education or who may require counselling and refer them to relevant community programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There are now more than 1,200 YRCP volunteers, who have reached out to more than 15,000 families.

sections.label: FRCs assisted inmate families
sections.summary: The FRCs have assisted close to 4,000 inmate families in the last two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The FRCs have assisted close to 4,000 inmate families in the last two years.

sections.label: Assessment of programmes for inmate families
sections.summary: Prisons' professional assessment is that programmes helped families with a positive attitude, and future measurement will be considered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: While no specific quantification has been done, Prisons' professional assessment, based on the interactions, is that the programmes have helped the families which have a positive attitude towards receiving such help.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: When they next assess, I will ask them to consider again whether there are ways in which some kind of measurement be done, either now or in the future because we are also talking about children growing up to be adults.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I did ask Mr Perera whether he agreed to the approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I certainly do agree that penalties have a critical role to play to control the supply and availability of drugs, as the Minister has explained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Rehabilitative approaches and preventive and early intervention programmes, such as what the Minister has explained, also have a critical role to play as well.
